definition_zh: 完美的；理想的；完全的；使完善；完成时
definition_en: having no fault and being as good as possible; exactly suitable; complete in every way; to make something fully developed
core_image: 一块被反复打磨的木头，棱角全部消失，表面能照出人的影子
scene: 木工房里，老师傅换掉最后一道砂纸，用指腹顺着木纹摸了一遍。He kept sanding until the surface felt perfect under his fingers.
sceneCN: 这里 perfect 是「完美的、无可挑剔的」（第 1 个义项：质地没有任何缺陷）；句意是他不肯停手，直到指腹摸到的表面毫无瑕疵。

derivatives.zh: 由 perfect 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「完美；完善」
由 perfect 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「完美地；完全地」
由否定前缀 im- 加 perfect 构成，义为「不完美的」
由 perfection 加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「完美主义者」

senses.title: Flawless in quality
senses.definition: so good in every detail that no fault can be found
senses.definitionCN: 每个细节都好到挑不出毛病
senses.example: Her piano playing is almost perfect.
senses.exampleCN: 她的钢琴演奏几乎无可挑剔。
senses.why: Perfectus is the past participle of a verb meaning to finish thoroughly, so the adjective first says finished, then finished so well that nothing at all is missing.
senses.whyCN: perfectus 本是一个意为「彻底做完」的动词的过去分词，所以这个形容词先说「做完了」，再说「做完到一点都不缺」，于是成了无可挑剔。

senses.title: Exactly suitable
senses.definition: the best possible thing for a particular purpose or person
senses.definitionCN: 对某个用途或某个人来说最合适的那一个
senses.example: The little courtyard is perfect for summer evenings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小院子最适合夏夜。
senses.why: Once a thing is complete, it meets its purpose with nothing left over and nothing short, so the word slides from nothing lacking to nothing mismatched.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西一旦完整，就恰好满足它的用途，既不多余也不欠缺，于是词义从「什么都不缺」滑到「什么都不错配」。

senses.title: Complete, used for emphasis
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean complete, often when someone is surprised or annoyed
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前表示「完全的」，常带惊讶或恼火的语气
senses.example: I felt like a perfect fool.
senses.exampleCN: 我觉得自己十足是个傻瓜。
senses.why: The old sense of thoroughly done survives here as bare emphasis: nothing is added to the noun except the claim that it is complete all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 「彻底做完」这个旧义在这里变成纯粹的强调：名词之外没有增加任何内容，只多了一句「从头到尾都够彻底」。

senses.title: To make something fully developed
senses.definition: to improve something through repeated work until it reaches its best possible form
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复打磨把某物改进到它能达到的最好状态
senses.example: She perfected her accent by listening to recordings.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠听录音把自己的口音打磨得很地道。
senses.why: The verb keeps the Latin prefix per-, meaning through, and so exposes the work hidden inside the adjective: carrying a thing through to the end.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语前缀 per-（穿过、彻底），因此把形容词里藏着的过程露了出来：把一件事一直做到头。

senses.title: The tense of completed action
senses.definition: the verb form that presents an action as finished rather than still going on
senses.definitionCN: 把动作呈现为已经完成、而不是仍在进行的动词形式
senses.example: In the perfect tense, the sentence uses have plus a past participle.
senses.exampleCN: 在完成时里，句子用 have 加过去分词。
senses.why: Grammarians took perfectus in its literal sense of finished and applied it to a verb form whose whole job is to say that an action is done.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家取 perfectus 字面上的「已完成」，把它安在一种专门表示动作已经做完的动词形式上。

intro.en: Perfect is built from two Latin pieces, a prefix meaning through and a verb meaning to make, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: perfect 由两个拉丁成分拼成，一个意为「彻底」的前缀，一个意为「做」的动词，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: The verb perficere joined per-, through, to facere, to do or make: to carry something through to the end.
items.cn: 动词 perficere 由表「穿过、彻底」的 per- 与 facere（做、造）组合，意为把一件事做到底。

items.en: Its past participle perfectus meant thoroughly made or finished, and only later gathered the sense of excellent quality.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 perfectus 意为「彻底做成的、完成的」，后来才带上称赞质量的意思。

items.en: Old French inherited the word as parfait, keeping both the sense of finished and the sense of excellent.
items.cn: 古法语继承为 parfait，把「完成」与「出色」两层意思一并保留。

items.en: Middle English took the adjective from French, and later formed a verb from the same stem, so one spelling now does two jobs.
items.cn: 中古英语从法语借入形容词，后来又用同一词干造出动词，于是一个拼写承担两种词性。

items.en: Modern English keeps the two apart only by stress: the adjective is stressed first, the verb last, and the spelling never shows it.
items.cn: 现代英语只靠重音区分二者：形容词前重，动词后重，而拼写完全看不出来。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the word family built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects adjectives that describe something without fault.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词族；近义组收表示「没有缺陷」的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being perfect, or the act of making something perfect.
entries.definitionCN: 完美的状态，或使某物完善的行为。

entries.definition: Having faults or missing parts, the direct opposite of the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 有缺陷或缺部分的，正好是形容词的反面。

entries.definition: The adverb made from perfect, meaning in a flawless or complete way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 perfect 构成的副词，意为完美地或完全地。

entries.definition: A person who is not satisfied with anything below a perfect standard.
entries.definitionCN: 对达不到完美标准的东西就不满意的人。

entries.definition: Without any fault, crack or weakness at all.
entries.definitionCN: 完全没有缺点、裂痕或弱点的。

entries.definition: The best that can be imagined for a purpose, rather than one that exists.
entries.definitionCN: 对某个用途而言能想象到的最好状态，而非已经存在的。

entries.definition: Showing no mistake, used especially of performance and technique.
entries.definitionCN: 没有失误的，尤用于表演与技术。

entries.definition: Complete in skill, carried to the highest level by long practice.
entries.definitionCN: 技艺炉火纯青的，经过长期练习达到最高水平。

normalIntro.en: The word divides into a prefix of thoroughness and a Latin verb of making, and its grammar sense comes from the same picture of a finished job.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词可拆成表「彻底」的前缀与表「做」的拉丁动词，它的语法义项也来自「活干完了」这个同一幅画面。

normal.en: Per- in perficere means through, and facere means make, so perfect starts life as made through and through.
normal.cn: perficere 里的 per- 意为穿过，facere 意为做，所以 perfect 的起点是「里外都做透」。

normal.en: The element -fect is a worn form of facere, and the same piece sits in defect, effect and infect, all about doing or making.
normal.cn: -fect 是 facere 磨损后的样子，同一成分也出现在 defect、effect、infect 里，都与做、造成有关。

normal.en: The adjective and the verb differ only in stress: the first syllable carries the describing sense, the second the acting one.
normal.cn: 形容词与动词只差重音：重音在前是「完美的」，在后是「使完美」。

normal.en: Practice makes perfect uses the adjective in its oldest sense, finished by repeated work rather than lucky from the start.
normal.cn: practice makes perfect 用的是形容词最老的意思：靠反复练习做出来的完成，而不是天生的好运。

normal.en: Add -ion and you get perfection, the state of having nothing left to improve.
normal.cn: 加上 -ion 就得到 perfection，即再也没有可改进之处的状态。

abstract.en: A surface polished until no scratch catches the light is the whole idea of the adjective in one glance.
abstract.cn: 一块磨到任何划痕都不反光的表面，一眼就能说明这个形容词的全部意思。

abstract.en: The verb is the hand still moving over that surface, which is why the same letters hold both the result and the work.
abstract.cn: 动词是仍在那块表面上移动的手，所以同样的字母既装得下结果，也装得下过程。

abstract.en: Grammar borrowed the word because a finished action and a flawless object share one picture: nothing left over, nothing missing.
abstract.cn: 语法借用了这个词，因为「做完的动作」与「无瑕的物件」共用一幅画面：没有多余，也没有欠缺。

examples.en: Her piano playing is almost perfect.
examples.cn: 她的钢琴演奏几乎无可挑剔。

examples.en: She perfected her accent by listening to recordings.
examples.cn: 她靠听录音把自己的口音打磨得很地道。

examples.en: The old table is still in perfect condition.
examples.cn: 这张旧桌子依然完好无损。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「颇费刻」——颇费功夫去雕刻，才刻得出完美的作品。

root: 拉丁语 per-（彻底）+ facere（做、造）→ perficere（做完）→ perfectus（完成的、完美的）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a job done all the way through; from that grow the ideas of flawlessness, exact fit, plain emphasis, the act of improving, and the grammar of finished action.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「一件事被做透」；无可挑剔、恰好合适、纯粹强调、使之完善以及完成时，都从这里长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a piece of wood sanded until no edge is left and the surface mirrors a face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被反复打磨的木头，棱角全部消失，表面能照出人的影子。

branches.en: a mirror surface with no scratch in it
branches.cn: 没有一道划痕的镜面

branches.en: a key that turns without the least resistance
branches.cn: 毫不费力就转开的钥匙

branches.en: a stranger who knows nobody in the room
branches.cn: 屋里谁也不认识的陌生人

branches.en: a hand going back over the same board once more
branches.cn: 在同一块板上又走一遍的手

branches.en: a sentence that reports a thing as already done
branches.cn: 把事说成已经做完的句子

intro.en: A Latin prefix of thoroughness and a Latin verb of making hold the whole family together, from the adjective to the grammar term.
intro.cn: 一个表「彻底」的拉丁前缀与一个表「做」的拉丁动词撑起整族词，从形容词一直到语法术语。

latinIntro.en: Perficere, perfectus and facere are all recorded Latin forms; the only doubtful point is how early the praising sense appeared in French.
latinIntro.cn: perficere、perfectus、facere 都是有记载的拉丁形式；唯一存疑之处是「称赞」这层意思在法语里出现得多早。

definition_zh: 完美地；完全地；恰好；十足地
definition_en: in a way that has no fault; completely, with nothing left out; in exactly the right way
core_image: 一只摆正的天平，两边砝码分毫不差，指针停在正中
scene: 面点师把烤盘从炉里取出，切开一角看了看内部的气孔。The loaf had risen perfectly, with an even crumb from edge to centre.
sceneCN: 这里 perfectly 是「完美地、毫无瑕疵地」（第 1 个义项）；句意为面包发得恰到好处，从边缘到中心的孔洞都均匀。

pos.zh: 完美地；完全地；恰好；十足地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「完美的」
由 perfect 加 -ion 构成，义为「完美；完善」
由否定前缀 im- 加 perfect 构成，义为「不完美的」

senses.title: In a flawless way
senses.definition: in a way that shows no fault, mistake or rough edge
senses.definitionCN: 以挑不出毛病、失误或毛糙之处的方式
senses.example: She sang the last note perfectly.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一个音她唱得完美无缺。
senses.why: The adverb simply adds the native ending -ly to the adjective, so it describes the manner of an action: the manner of something without fault.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是在形容词后加上本族词尾 -ly，因此描述动作的方式：以没有缺陷的方式去做。

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: used with adjectives to mean completely, with no part or condition left out
senses.definitionCN: 与形容词连用，表示完全、没有任何部分或条件被遗漏
senses.example: Make sure the wound is perfectly clean before you bandage it.
senses.exampleCN: 包扎之前一定要让伤口彻底清洁。
senses.why: A thing that is perfect has nothing missing, and when the word is put before an adjective that completeness turns into plain intensity: clean all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 完美的东西什么都不缺，当这个词放在形容词前时，那份完整就变成纯粹的强度：从头到尾都干净。

senses.title: Exactly, just right
senses.definition: in exactly the right way, at exactly the right moment or in exactly the right place
senses.definitionCN: 方式、时机或位置都正好合适
senses.example: The trap was perfectly placed under the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 陷阱安放在落叶下面，位置恰到好处。
senses.why: Perfect fit is the middle sense of the adjective, and the adverb makes it about timing and placing: neither too early nor too far, but exactly on the mark.
senses.whyCN: 「恰好合适」是形容词居中的一层意思，副词把它落到时机与位置上：不早不晚、不远不近，正好在点上。

senses.title: Very, as spoken emphasis
senses.definition: used in conversation to strengthen a judgement, close to very or quite
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中加强判断，意思接近 very 或 quite
senses.example: It is perfectly good bread, so do not throw it away.
senses.exampleCN: 这面包完全够好，别扔掉。
senses.why: In speech the word drifts from an objective judgement to a speaker's stance, so perfectly good is not a claim of flawlessness but a mild protest against waste.
senses.whyCN: 在口语里这个词从客观判断滑向说话人的态度，所以 perfectly good 不是宣称毫无瑕疵，而是对浪费轻轻表示反对。

intro.en: The adverb is younger than the adjective: English took perfect from French and then built perfectly with a native ending.
intro.cn: 副词比形容词年轻：英语先从法语借入 perfect，再用本族词尾造出 perfectly。

items.en: The adjective came first, meaning thoroughly finished, and it travelled into French rather than straight into English.
items.cn: 先有形容词，意为彻底完成，它是经法语而不是直接传入英语的。

items.en: Old French parfait carried both the sense of complete and the sense of excellent into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 parfait 把「完成」与「出色」两层意思一起带进中古英语。

items.en: Middle English used perfect as an adjective of quality, and the adverb was later formed from it inside English.
items.cn: 中古英语把 perfect 用作表示性质的形容词，副词是后来在英语内部由它构成的。

items.en: The ending behind -ly was Old English -lice, meaning in the manner of, so perfectly means in a perfect manner.
items.cn: -ly 的前身是古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」，所以 perfectly 即「以完美的方式」。

items.en: Modern English widened the adverb from manner to degree, so perfectly can now mean completely or very as well.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个副词从「方式」扩展到「程度」，于是 perfectly 也能表示完全或非常。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the word family sharing the same stem and ending; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of completeness and precision.
note.cn: 形近组收共用同一词干与词尾的词族；近义组收表示「完全」与「精确」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective and verb that perfectly is built on.
entries.definitionCN: perfectly 由之构成的形容词与动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being perfect.
entries.definitionCN: 表示完美状态的名词。

entries.definition: Having faults, the direct opposite of the base adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 有缺陷的，正好是基础形容词的反面。

entries.definition: A person who demands a standard nothing can fall short of.
entries.definitionCN: 要求达到一个不容打折的标准的人。

entries.definition: To the fullest degree, with nothing left out.
entries.definitionCN: 达到最大程度，什么都不缺。

entries.definition: As a whole, without exception or remainder.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体，没有例外或剩余。

entries.definition: In precise agreement with a fact, measure or instruction.
entries.definitionCN: 与事实、量度或指示精确相符。

entries.definition: With attention to every part, leaving nothing half done.
entries.definitionCN: 顾及每一部分，不留半成品。

entries.definition: Without limit or condition, often used to strengthen a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 没有限制或条件，常用来加强说法。

normalIntro.en: Perfectly is the adjective plus a native ending that names a manner, and English later let that manner stretch into degree.
normalIntro.cn: perfectly 是形容词加一个表「方式」的本族词尾，英语后来让这种「方式」延伸到「程度」。

normal.en: Perfectly is perfect plus -ly, and -ly turns a quality into the way something is done.
normal.cn: perfectly 是 perfect 加 -ly，而 -ly 把性质变成做事的方式。

normal.en: The -ly ending goes back to Old English -lice, which literally meant in the manner of.
normal.cn: -ly 可上溯到古英语 -lice，字面意思就是「以……的方式」。

normal.en: Because a flawless manner and a complete degree sit close together, perfectly easy and perfectly timed both sound natural.
normal.cn: 因为「无瑕的方式」与「十足的程度」贴得很近，perfectly easy 与 perfectly timed 听起来都很自然。

normal.en: Perfectly clear is a common phrase in speech, often said when someone has failed to understand.
normal.cn: perfectly clear 是口语里的常见说法，往往是在对方没听懂时说的。

normal.en: The adverb never takes -er: English says more perfectly, not perfectlier.
normal.cn: 这个副词从不加 -er：英语说 more perfectly，不说 perfectlier。

abstract.en: A balance with the pointer resting exactly in the middle is the adverb in one picture.
abstract.cn: 一只指针正好停在中间的天平，就是这个副词的一幅画像。

abstract.en: Perfection is a state, perfectly is the way of acting that reaches it, and a small ending carries that whole claim.
abstract.cn: 完美是一种状态，perfectly 是抵达它的行动方式，一个小小的词尾就承载了整个主张。

abstract.en: When speakers say perfectly good, the word stops measuring quality and starts pressing a point.
abstract.cn: 当人们说 perfectly good 时，这个词不再衡量质量，而是在强调一个立场。

examples.en: She sang the last note perfectly.
examples.cn: 最后一个音她唱得完美无缺。

examples.en: Make sure the wound is perfectly clean before you bandage it.
examples.cn: 包扎之前一定要让伤口彻底清洁。

examples.en: The trap was perfectly placed under the leaves.
examples.cn: 陷阱安放在落叶下面，位置恰到好处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「颇费克特利」——颇费力气去磨，才换来一点完美。

root: perfect（完美的）加本族副词词尾 -ly；perfect 来自拉丁语 perfectus（彻底完成的）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is doing something in a flawless manner; from that grow the senses of complete degree, exact fit, and spoken emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「以无瑕的方式做事」；完全的程度、恰好合适以及口语强调都从这里长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance levelled exactly, the pointer resting in the middle with equal weights on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只摆正的天平，两边砝码相等，指针停在正中。

branches.en: a note held clean to the very end
branches.cn: 干干净净唱到结尾的一个音

branches.en: a wound washed until no grit is left
branches.cn: 洗到没有一粒沙的伤口

branches.en: a trap set on the one soft patch of ground
branches.cn: 安在唯一一处软土上的陷阱

branches.en: a train arriving as the doors close
branches.cn: 车门关上时刚好进站的列车

branches.en: a loaf of bread defended against the bin
branches.cn: 被人从垃圾桶边上救回来的面包

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin participle, an English adjective, and two native endings that shift a quality into a manner and a state.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁分词、英语形容词以及两个本族词尾撑起，后两个词尾把一个性质分别变成方式和状态。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base perfectus is well recorded; the adverb itself is an English formation, so no Latin adverb needs to be assumed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础形式 perfectus 有可靠记载；副词本身是英语的构造，无须假设一个拉丁副词。

definition_zh: 表演；演出；执行；做；表现；履行
definition_en: to present a play, piece of music or dance to an audience; to carry out a task or operation; to work in a particular way as judged by results
core_image: 聚光灯下的舞台，演员从侧幕走出，把练过无数遍的动作一次做完
scene: 剧院的后台挤满人，化妆镜前的灯泡亮着，开场铃已经响过。The whole cast performed without a single missed cue.
sceneCN: 这里 perform 是「表演、演出」（第 1 个义项）；句意为整台演员演下来，没有漏掉任何一个提示点。

derivatives.zh: 由 perform 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「表演；表现；性能」
由 perform 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「表演者」
由 perform 加 -ing 构成，义为「表演的」，如表演艺术

senses.title: To act before an audience
senses.definition: to present a play, concert, dance or other show to people who are watching
senses.definitionCN: 把戏剧、音乐会、舞蹈等演给观众看
senses.example: The band performed three new songs.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队演唱了三首新歌。
senses.why: The French source meant to carry something through to the end, so a show that is carried through in front of an audience is exactly what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为「把一件事做到底」，于是一场在观众面前从头做到尾的演出，正好就是这个词所描述的。

senses.title: To carry out a task
senses.definition: to do a task, action or operation, especially one that needs skill or care
senses.definitionCN: 做一项任务、行动或手术，尤指需要技巧或细心的
senses.example: Surgeons performed the operation in under two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生在不到两小时内完成了手术。
senses.why: The French source is about finishing a piece of business, and a task or an operation is exactly such a piece of work: it exists only to be carried through.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源说的是把一桩事务做完，而一项任务或一台手术正是这样的活儿：它存在就是为了被做完。

senses.title: To show how well you work
senses.definition: to work or function in a particular way, as judged by the results produced
senses.definitionCN: 按产生的成果来评判，以某种方式工作或运转
senses.example: The team performed well under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在压力下表现出色。
senses.why: Once the verb means carrying work through, it can also describe how that carrying went, so the results become part of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示把活儿做到底，它也能描述做得怎么样，于是成绩本身就成了一层词义。

senses.title: To fulfil a duty or promise
senses.definition: to do what you have promised to do or what your position requires
senses.definitionCN: 去做你承诺过的事，或你的职位要求你做的事
senses.example: The company failed to perform its duties under the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 公司未能履行合同规定的义务。
senses.why: A duty is the clearest case of something that exists only in order to be done, so the oldest sense of completing an obligation survives here almost unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 职责最能说明「存在就是为了被完成」的东西，所以「完成义务」这一最老的意思几乎原样留了下来。

intro.en: The usual account takes perform from Old French parfournir, to supply completely, with the intensifying par- related to Latin per-.
intro.cn: 一般认为 perform 来自古法语 parfournir（彻底提供），其中加强语气的 par- 与拉丁语 per- 有关。

items.en: The French verb fournir meant to supply or provide, and it supplies the second half of the English word.
items.cn: 法语动词 fournir 意为供给、提供，构成了这个词的后半截。

items.en: Parfournir added an intensifying par- and meant to complete or carry out fully; this is the source usually given for the English verb.
items.cn: parfournir 加上表彻底的 par-，意为完成、彻底履行；这通常被认为是英语动词的来源。

items.en: Anglo-Norman records used the verb for completing a task, an obligation or a piece of business.
items.cn: 盎格鲁—诺曼时期的文书记用这个动词，指完成一项任务、义务或一桩事务。

items.en: Middle English extended it from finishing a duty to presenting a play, since both are carried through to the end.
items.cn: 中古英语把它从「完成义务」扩展到「上演戏剧」，因为两者都要一直做到结尾。

items.en: Modern English keeps the three main uses side by side: a show on stage, a task in hand, and a level of results.
items.cn: 现代英语把三条主要用法并列保留：舞台上的演出、手上的任务，以及成绩的高低。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and adjective branches of the same verb; the near-meaning group collects verbs of carrying something out.
note.cn: 形近组收同一动词的名词与形容词分支；近义组收表示「把事做出来」的动词。

entries.definition: The act of performing, or how well someone or something works.
entries.definitionCN: 表演这一行为，或某人某物运转得好不好。

entries.definition: A person who performs for an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 为观众表演的人。

entries.definition: The adjective used in phrases such as performing arts.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表演艺术这类短语的形容词。

entries.definition: To do something, or to play a role on stage.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事，或在舞台上扮演角色。

entries.definition: To carry out a plan, order or difficult movement with skill.
entries.definitionCN: 有技巧地执行计划、命令或高难动作。

entries.definition: To organize and carry out an activity such as a study or a ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 组织并实施研究、仪式之类的活动。

entries.definition: To arrange and present a play or event for an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 为观众安排并上演戏剧或活动。

normalIntro.en: The French source says supply completely, so the word keeps returning to the idea of delivering a whole thing, whether a song, an operation or a duty.
normalIntro.cn: 法语来源意为「彻底提供」，所以这个词反复回到「把整件事交付出来」这个意思，无论是一首歌、一台手术还是一份职责。

normal.en: The French source means to provide fully, so perform is about delivering the whole thing rather than a part of it.
normal.cn: 法语来源意为「完整地提供」，所以 perform 讲的是把整件事交付出来，而不是只做一部分。

normal.en: Performance adds -ance, the ending that turns a verb of doing into the doing itself.
normal.cn: performance 加 -ance，这个词尾把「做」的动词变成「做」这件事本身。

normal.en: Performer adds -er, and the result is the person who delivers the thing.
normal.cn: performer 加 -er，得到的就是那个把东西交付出来的人。

normal.en: A play is performed, an operation is performed and a duty is performed: the same verb covers all three because each is carried through.
normal.cn: 戏可以 perform，手术可以 perform，职责也可以 perform：同一个动词能管三件事，因为都要做到底。

normal.en: Perform well asks about results, perform live asks about an audience, so what follows the verb decides which sense is active.
normal.cn: perform well 问的是成绩，perform live 说的是有没有观众，所以动词后面接什么决定了哪一层意思在起作用。

abstract.en: A cue sheet backstage and a checklist in an operating room share one word, because both list steps that must be carried out in order.
abstract.cn: 后台的提示单与手术室里的核对表共用一个词，因为两者列的都是必须按顺序做完的步骤。

abstract.en: The word treats a concert, an operation and a promise as the same shape: something begun, done and finished in front of others.
abstract.cn: 这个词把音乐会、手术和承诺看成同一个形状：开始、做完，并在别人面前收尾。

abstract.en: When we say a machine performs, we quietly compare it to a performer judged by the audience.
abstract.cn: 当我们说一台机器 perform 时，其实是在悄悄把它比作一个被观众评判的表演者。

examples.en: The band performed three new songs.
examples.cn: 乐队演唱了三首新歌。

examples.en: Surgeons performed the operation in under two hours.
examples.cn: 外科医生在不到两小时内完成了手术。

examples.en: The team performed well under pressure.
examples.cn: 这支队伍在压力下表现出色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「颇费劲」——台上看着轻松，台下颇费劲；perform 是表演，也是把事做完。

root: 一般认为来自古法语 parfournir（彻底提供、完成）：par- 与拉丁语 per-（彻底）同源，fournir 意为提供。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is carrying something through to the end; a show, a task, a set of results and a duty are four places where that completion becomes visible.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「把一件事一直做到结尾」；演出、任务、成绩与职责，是这种「做完」显现出来的四个场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an actor stepping out of the wings under a spotlight and finishing a routine rehearsed a hundred times.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚光灯下，演员从侧幕走出，把练过上百遍的动作一次做完。

branches.en: a curtain rising on a full house
branches.cn: 满座剧场里升起的幕布

branches.en: a checklist ticked off step by step
branches.cn: 一项项打勾的核对表

branches.en: a scoreboard read after the final whistle
branches.cn: 终场哨响后被人查看的记分牌

branches.en: a signed contract laid on a desk
branches.cn: 摊在桌上的一份签字合同

branches.en: a review that judges both the show and the skill
branches.cn: 同时评判演出与技艺的评论

intro.en: An Old French verb of supplying, an intensifying prefix and three English endings carry the word from an act to a person, a result and a field of art.
intro.cn: 一个表「供给」的古法语动词、一个加强前缀以及三个英语词尾，把这个词从行为带到人、结果与艺术领域。

latinIntro.en: Only the prefix is Latin: par- traces back to per-. The French verb fournir has no Latin original, which is why the Latin list stays short.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前缀是拉丁成分：par- 可上溯到 per-。法语动词 fournir 没有拉丁原型，所以拉丁同源词列得很短。

definition_zh: 表演；演出；表现；业绩；执行；履行；性能；语言运用；（仪式的）进行；表演性
definition_en: the act of staging a work for an audience, the way a person, team, or machine carries out a task, the fulfilling of a duty, or the actual use of language as opposed to underlying knowledge
core_image: 舞台上的动作被观众看见并打分，或机器被推到极限，看它到底能跑多快
scene: 年终评审会上，经理把三条产品线的曲线投在墙上，逐条解释哪一条达标。The manager put the performance curves of three product lines on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 performance 是「业绩」（第 2 个义项：个人或组织在工作上取得的成果与表现）；句意：经理把三条产品线的业绩曲线投在墙上；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 表演；演出；表现；业绩；执行；履行；性能

derivatives.zh: 表演；执行；履行；运转
表演者；执行者
施为性的；表演性的
表演性；施为性
表现不佳；业绩低于预期

senses.title: A work staged for an audience
senses.definition: the staging of a play, concert, dance, or other work before an audience, taken as an event or an art
senses.definitionCN: 在观众面前上演戏剧、音乐会、舞蹈或其他作品，作为事件或艺术看待
senses.example: The evening performance sold out two weeks in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 晚场演出提前两周售罄。
senses.why: The Old French source meant 'to complete, to carry through'. A play is complete only when it is carried through in front of people: the script is the plan, performance is the doing.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源意为“完成、贯彻到底”。一部戏只有在人前贯彻到底才算完成：剧本是计划，performance 是做出来。

senses.title: How well a person or group does
senses.definition: the measured quality of a person's, team's, or organization's work against a standard or expectation
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团队或组织的工作相对于标准或预期的可衡量质量
senses.example: Her performance improved once the targets were made clear.
senses.exampleCN: 目标明确之后，她的表现有所提升。
senses.why: The same carrying-through is now watched by a manager rather than an audience. What matters is not whether the work is beautiful but whether it reaches the mark.
senses.whyCN: 同样是贯彻到底，只是这次看的是经理而不是观众。关键不再是作品美不美，而是它有没有达到标准。

senses.title: The carrying out of a task
senses.definition: the act of executing a task, duty, or function, often with attention to whether it was done at all and done correctly
senses.definitionCN: 执行任务、职责或功能的行为，常关注是否完成以及是否正确完成
senses.example: The performance of the repair took longer than the estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项维修的执行比预估花了更长时间。
senses.why: This is the plainest sense: the plan is carried through. No audience and no score, only the difference between what was supposed to happen and what happened.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的义项：计划被贯彻到底。没有观众也没有评分，只有“本该发生什么”与“实际发生了什么”之间的差别。

senses.title: What a machine can do
senses.definition: the speed, power, or efficiency with which a machine, vehicle, or system operates under test or load
senses.definitionCN: 机器、车辆或系统在测试或负载下运转的速度、功率或效率
senses.example: The engine's performance drops at high altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机在高海拔地区性能会下降。
senses.why: A machine has no will, but it can still be pushed to its limit. Performance becomes the measure of that limit, the carrying-through of metal instead of muscle.
senses.whyCN: 机器没有意志，但仍可被推到极限。performance 成了对这种极限的度量，是金属而非肌肉的贯彻到底。

senses.title: Actual use of language
senses.definition: in linguistics, the actual production and comprehension of speech in real situations, as opposed to the speaker's underlying competence
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中指真实情境中话语的实际产生与理解，相对于说话者底层的语言能力
senses.example: Errors in performance do not prove a lack of competence.
senses.exampleCN: 语言运用中的错误并不能证明缺乏语言能力。
senses.why: Chomsky borrowed the word for the difference between knowing a grammar and using it under pressure. The plan inside the head is competence; the carrying-through in time is performance.
senses.whyCN: 乔姆斯基借这个词区分“懂语法”与“在压力下使用语法”。头脑里的计划是语言能力，时间中的贯彻到底是语言运用。

senses.title: One particular show
senses.definition: a single instance of presenting a work, countable and datable, as in the third performance of a run
senses.definitionCN: 呈现某作品的一次具体实例，可计数、可定时，如巡演中的第三场
senses.example: The Saturday performance was recorded for the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 周六那场演出被录入了档案。
senses.why: A run of a play is many carryings-through. This sense counts them, which is why the word takes a plural and a date while the art sense does not.
senses.whyCN: 一部戏的连演是许多次贯彻到底。这个义项把它们数出来，所以这个词可以有复数和日期，而艺术义则不行。

senses.title: The carrying out of a ritual
senses.definition: the enactment of a ceremony, rite, or formal role according to prescribed words and actions
senses.definitionCN: 按规定的言语与动作进行仪式、典礼或正式角色
senses.example: The performance of the wedding rite lasted forty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼仪式的进行持续了四十分钟。
senses.why: A rite exists only when it is done. Here performance is not entertainment but the condition of the thing existing at all, which shows how wide the 'carry through' sense is.
senses.whyCN: 仪式只有在被做出来时才存在。这里的 performance 不是娱乐，而是事物得以存在的条件，可见“贯彻到底”这一义项有多宽。

senses.title: The financial results of a business
senses.definition: the financial results of a company, fund, or economy over a period, measured in profit, growth, or return
senses.definitionCN: 公司、基金或经济在一段时间内的财务结果，以利润、增长或回报衡量
senses.example: The fund's performance trailed the index for three quarters.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金连续三个季度的业绩落后于指数。
senses.why: Money is the scoreboard of the market. Performance here is the carrying-through of a strategy expressed as a number that can be compared with rivals.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是市场的记分牌。这里的 performance 是把战略贯彻到底后，用可与对手比较的数字表达出来的结果。

senses.title: Doing that makes what it says
senses.definition: the quality of an utterance or act that brings about what it describes, as when saying 'I promise' is itself the promise
senses.definitionCN: 话语或行为在说出或做出时同时实现其所描述之事的性质，例如说“我保证”本身就是保证
senses.example: The philosopher studied the performative side of promises and apologies.
senses.exampleCN: 这位哲学家研究承诺与道歉的施为性一面。
senses.why: If a promise is completed by being spoken, then the saying is the doing. This sense pushes the 'carry through' idea to its limit: the performance is the only thing there is.
senses.whyCN: 如果承诺因被说出而完成，那么说就是做。这个义项把“贯彻到底”推到极限：表演本身就是唯一存在的东西。

intro.en: Performance comes from perform plus -ance (Latin -antia). Perform is not built on form: it comes from Anglo-French parformer, from Old French parfournir 'to accomplish, complete', literally per- 'thoroughly' + fournir 'to provide, furnish'. The original sense is 'to carry something through to the end'. English added the theatre sense in the 16th century, the machine sense in the 19th, and the linguistic sense in the 20th.
intro.cn: performance 来自 perform 加 -ance（拉丁 -antia）。perform 并不是由 form 构成的：它来自盎格鲁法语 parformer，再上溯古法语 parfournir“完成、贯彻”，字面是 per-“彻底”+ fournir“提供、供给”。本义是“把某事贯彻到底”。英语在 16 世纪加入戏剧义，19 世纪加入机器义，20 世纪加入语言学义。

items.en: Parfournir means 'to complete, to carry out fully'. The prefix par- is the French form of Latin per- 'thoroughly'; fournir 'to furnish, provide' is from the reconstructed Frankish form *frumjan.
items.cn: parfournir 意为“完成、彻底执行”。前缀 par- 是拉丁 per-“彻底”的法语形式；fournir“供给、提供”出自法兰克语的重构形式 *frumjan。

items.en: English perform first means 'to carry out, accomplish, execute' a task, promise, or duty. The spelling has no connection with form, despite the shared letters.
items.cn: 英语 perform 最早意为“执行、完成、履行”任务、承诺或职责。尽管拼写共享 form 几个字母，它与 form 毫无词源关系。

items.en: The theatre sense develops: to perform a play is to carry the script through into sound and action before an audience.
items.cn: 戏剧义在 16 世纪发展出来：演一部戏，就是把剧本贯彻成观众面前的声与动作。

items.en: Industry applies the word to machines and horses: performance is what an engine or animal can actually deliver under load.
items.cn: 19 世纪工业把这个词用于机器与马匹：performance 是发动机或牲畜在负载下实际能交付的东西。

items.en: Chomsky contrasts performance with competence in linguistics (1965), and management makes performance a measurable target.
items.cn: 20 世纪乔姆斯基在语言学中用 performance 与 competence 相对（1965），管理学则把 performance 变成可测量的指标。

items.en: Form, formal, and formative come from Latin forma 'shape'. Perform has no forma inside it: its fournir is 'provide'. The shared form- is spelling only, so performance is completion, not shaping.
items.cn: form、formal、formative 来自拉丁 forma“形状”。perform 里面没有 forma：它的 fournir 是“提供”。共享的 form- 只是拼写，所以 performance 是完成，不是塑形。

note.en: The first group separates perform's true family from the form trap. The second group compares execution, achievement, a show, and efficiency, the four words most often used in place of performance.
note.cn: 第一组把 perform 真正的词族与 form 陷阱分开。第二组比较执行、成就、演出与效率，这四个词最常被用来替代 performance。

entries.definition: to carry out an action, duty, or work before others. Performance is the noun of that carrying-through.
entries.definitionCN: 执行某项行动、职责或在他人面前呈现作品。performance 是这一贯彻过程的名称。

entries.definition: a person who performs, especially on stage. It names the doer, while performance names the deed or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 表演的人，尤指舞台上的人。它命名做的人，而 performance 命名行为或其结果。

entries.definition: shape, structure, or a document with blanks. It comes from Latin forma 'shape' and has no connection with perform's fournir 'provide'.
entries.definitionCN: 形状、结构，或带空格的表格。它来自拉丁 forma“形状”，与 perform 的 fournir“提供”毫无关系。

entries.definition: shaping someone's development, as in formative years. It belongs to the forma family, so it is about shaping, not about completing a task.
entries.definitionCN: 塑造人成长的，如“形成期”。它属于 forma 词族，讲的是塑形，不是完成任务。

entries.definition: the act of putting a plan, order, or law into effect. It is close to performance in the task sense but carries no audience or score.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划、命令或法律付诸实施的行为。它在任务义上接近 performance，但不带观众或评分。

entries.definition: something accomplished, especially after effort. It names the result that stands, while performance can name the ongoing doing.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力而完成的事。它命名留下来的结果，而 performance 可以命名正在进行的做。

entries.definition: a public entertainment, or a display. It is the event sense of performance, but it can also mean an insincere display.
entries.definitionCN: 公开的娱乐演出，或展示。它对应 performance 的事件义，但也可以指不真诚的做样子。

entries.definition: the ratio of useful output to the resources used. It is one measured part of performance, not the whole judgement of it.
entries.definitionCN: 有用产出与所耗资源之比。它是 performance 中被测量的一部分，而不是对它的整体判断。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: Old French parfournir, fournir 'provide', the 16th-century stage sense, the 19th-century machine sense, and the form trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：古法语 parfournir、fournir“提供”、16 世纪的舞台义、19 世纪的机器义，以及 form 陷阱。

normal.en: Parfournir is 'to complete': a performance is a plan carried through to the end, whether on a stage, in a factory, or under a test load.
normal.cn: parfournir 是“完成”：performance 就是被贯彻到底的计划，无论是在舞台上、车间里，还是在测试负载下。

normal.en: Perform has no form inside it; its fournir means 'provide'. The resemblance to form is a spelling accident.
normal.cn: perform 里面没有 form；它的 fournir 意为“提供”。与 form 的相似只是拼写上的偶然。

normal.en: Theatre gave the word its audience, industry gave it a dial, and linguistics gave it a contrast with competence.
normal.cn: 戏剧给了它观众，工业给了它仪表盘，语言学给了它与“语言能力”的对照。

normal.en: The suffix chain is perform → performer → performance → performative, with -ance naming the act or result.
normal.cn: 后缀链是 perform → performer → performance → performative，其中 -ance 命名行为或结果。

normal.en: A performance review, a live performance, and an engine's performance are the same noun doing three jobs: judgement, event, and limit.
normal.cn: 绩效评估、现场演出与发动机性能，是同一个名词在做三件事：评判、事件与极限。

abstract.en: A score is only a plan for sound; the concert exists for one hour and then cannot be returned to.
abstract.cn: 乐谱只是声音的计划；音乐会存在一小时，然后就再也回不去了。

abstract.en: A machine has no ambition, yet we ask it to perform, as if the dial could be proud.
abstract.cn: 机器没有野心，我们却要求它“表现”，仿佛仪表盘会骄傲。

abstract.en: Saying 'I promise' does not describe the promise; it is the promise, made in the air between two people.
abstract.cn: 说“我保证”并不是在描述承诺；它就是承诺本身，在两个人口之间的空气里做成。

examples.en: The orchestra's performance was broadcast to a million listeners.
examples.cn: 乐团的演出被播给上百万听众。

examples.en: The company reported strong performance in the third quarter.
examples.cn: 公司报告第三季度业绩强劲。

examples.en: The contract requires the performance of the work by June.
examples.cn: 合同要求这项工程在六月前完成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破佛曼斯」——演员“破”开剧本，把计划“佛”系地贯彻到底，站在台上做完 → performance 表演；表现；性能（只借音，不表词源）

root: 盎格鲁法语 parformer、古法语 parfournir「完成、贯彻到底」，由 per-「彻底」+ fournir「提供」构成；后缀 -ance（拉丁 -antia）构成名词。核心是「把计划贯彻到底，做到最后」。与 form（拉丁 forma「形状」）只是拼写相似，词根不同；四个主要义项分别是演出、表现、执行、性能。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of performance all describe a plan carried through to the end. What changes is who watches and what counts: an audience, a manager, a contract, a test bench, a grammar, a ritual, a market, or the very act of speaking.
sensesIntro.cn: performance 的九个义项都描述一个被贯彻到底的计划。变化的是谁在看、什么算数：观众、经理、合同、试验台、语法、仪式、市场，还是说话这一行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plan driven through to the end while others watch and judge the result.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个计划在他人注视与评判下被贯彻到底。

branches.en: THE STAGE AND THE RITE: a work or ceremony carried through before witnesses, and one countable instance of it.
branches.cn: 舞台与仪式：在见证者面前完成的艺术作品或典礼，以及其中可计数的一次。

branches.en: THE SCOREBOARD: a person's or firm's results measured against a standard, including financial results.
branches.cn: 记分牌：个人或公司相对标准的成果，包括财务结果。

branches.en: THE PLAIN DEED: a task or duty actually executed, with no audience beyond the contract.
branches.cn: 朴素的行为：实际执行的任务或职责，除合同外没有别的观众。

branches.en: THE MACHINE'S LIMIT: what an engine or system can deliver under load.
branches.cn: 机器的极限：发动机或系统在负载下能交付的东西。

branches.en: LANGUAGE AS DOING: actual speech use in contrast to competence, and utterances that accomplish what they say.
branches.cn: 作为行动的语言：与语言能力相对的实际言语运用，以及说出即做成的话语。

intro.en: Performance is perform plus -ance, from Latin -antia. Perform comes from Old French parfournir, not from form. The family is regular: -er the person, -ance the act or result, -ative the adjective, -ativity the abstract quality.
intro.cn: performance 是 perform 加 -ance（拉丁 -antia）。perform 来自古法语 parfournir，而不是 form。词族很规则：-er 人、-ance 行为或结果、-ative 形容词、-ativity 抽象性质。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is per- 'thoroughly' and the noun suffix -antia, which forms nouns of state or action. The verb itself is French, from Frankish *frumjan 'to provide'; Latin had no performare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 per-“彻底”与名词后缀 -antia（构成状态或动作名词）。动词本身是法语的，出自法兰克语 *frumjan“提供”；拉丁语并没有 performare 这个动词。

items.meaning: the carrying out of a task, or its public result
items.meaningCN: 任务的执行，或其公开的结果（-ance 动作／结果名词）
items.example: The performance of the pump was tested at low temperature.
items.exampleCN: 这台泵的性能在低温下接受了测试。

items.meaning: to carry out, complete, or present
items.example: The team performed the test twice.
items.exampleCN: 团队把这项测试做了两次。

items.meaning: one who performs, especially on stage
items.meaningCN: 表演的人，尤指舞台上的人（-er 施动者）
items.example: The performer left the stage in silence.
items.exampleCN: 表演者在沉默中离开舞台。

items.meaning: of an utterance that does what it says
items.meaningCN: 指说出即做成之话语的；施为性的（-ative 功能形容词）
items.example: A performative utterance changes the world by being said.
items.exampleCN: 施为性话语通过被说出而改变世界。

items.meaning: the capacity of acts or words to bring about what they name
items.meaningCN: 行为或言语产生其所命名之事的能力；表演性（-ity 性质名词）
items.example: Gender performativity is a key concept in that field.
items.exampleCN: 性别表演性是该领域的一个核心概念。

items.meaningCN: 低于预期标准的表现（under- 低于）
items.example: Underperformance cost the division its bonus.
items.exampleCN: 表现不佳让该部门失去了奖金。

items.meaningCN: 比对手做得更好（out- 超过）

items.meaning: shape or structure; not related to perform
items.meaningCN: 形状或结构；与 perform 不同源
items.example: The form of the roof follows the wind.
They furnished the room before the guests arrived.
items.exampleCN: 客人到达前他们布置好了房间。

latinEntries.meaning: state or action, forming abstract nouns
latinEntries.meaningCN: 状态或动作，构成抽象名词
形状、模子、形式（与 perform 无关）

derivatives.zh: 表演；执行；履行
表演者；执行者
施为性的；表演性的
表演性；施为性
表现不佳

definition_zh: 表演者；演员；演奏者；执行者；表现良好的人或物
definition_en: a person who acts, sings, dances or plays music for an audience; also a person or thing that carries out a task or reaches a particular level of results
core_image: 一束光落在舞台中央，一个人抬脚走进去，把练了千百遍的动作交给台下
scene: 演出开始前，幕布后面很安静，只有鞋底轻轻碰着地板的声音。The performer walked to the centre of the stage and the hall went quiet.
sceneCN: 这里是「表演者、演员」（第 1 个义项：为观众表演的人）；句意为表演者走到舞台中央，整个大厅随即安静下来。

pos.zh: 表演者；演员；演奏者；执行者；表现良好的人或物

derivatives.zh: 来自古法语 parfournir，义为「表演；执行；运转」
perform 加名词后缀 -ance，义为「表演；表现；性能」
perform 加 -ing 作形容词，义为「表演的；执行的」，如表演艺术
perform 加 -ative，义为「述行性的；与表演有关的」

senses.title: Someone who entertains an audience
senses.definition: a person who acts, sings, dances or plays music in front of an audience
senses.definitionCN: 在观众面前演戏、唱歌、跳舞或演奏音乐的人
senses.example: The performer held the audience for two hours without a break.
senses.exampleCN: 这位表演者让观众连着看了两个小时，中间没有休息。
senses.why: Perform first meant to carry a task through to the end; when the task is a song or a role done in public, the one who carries it out becomes the performer.
senses.whyCN: perform 最初指把事情做到最后；当被做到最后的东西是一支歌或一个角色，而且是在众人面前完成时，完成它的人就成了表演者。

senses.title: Someone who carries out a task
senses.definition: a person who does a piece of work or a duty, especially one that is hard or needs skill
senses.definitionCN: 完成某项工作或职责的人，尤指任务艰难或需要技巧时
senses.example: She is the quiet performer who finishes whatever the team plans.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那个不声不响的执行者，团队计划的事都由她做完。
senses.why: The stage sense grew out of the older sense of finishing a job, so the word still names anyone who actually gets the work done, even with no audience at all.
senses.whyCN: 舞台义是从「把活干完」这个更早的意思长出来的，所以这个词仍指真正把事情做完的人，哪怕台下根本没有观众。

senses.title: A person or thing that delivers results
senses.definition: a person, company or product that reaches a particular level of success or efficiency
senses.definitionCN: 达到某种成功程度或效率的人、公司或产品
senses.example: Reviewers called the small car a solid performer on long drives.
senses.exampleCN: 评测者称这款小车在长途行驶中表现可靠。
senses.why: Once performer names whoever completes an action, business writing extends it to anything judged by how well it acts, so a car or a company can be a good performer too.
senses.whyCN: 既然 performer 指把动作完成的人，商业语境就把它扩展到一切按「做得怎么样」来评价的对象，于是汽车或公司也能被称为表现良好者。

intro.en: Performer is the English verb perform plus the suffix -er; the verb itself came through Old French from a Frankish stem, with a Latin prefix at its head.
intro.cn: performer 是英语动词 perform 加后缀 -er 构成；动词本身经古法语来自法兰克语词干，词首则是一个拉丁语前缀。

items.en: The Latin prefix per- meant through or thoroughly, and it survives in the first syllable of the English verb.
items.cn: 拉丁语前缀 per- 意为「穿过、彻底」，保存在这个英语动词的第一个音节里。

items.en: The second element is usually traced to a reconstructed Frankish verb meaning to provide or accomplish; because the form is reconstructed, the source is not fully certain.
items.cn: 第二部分一般追溯到重构的法兰克语动词，意为「提供、完成」；由于该形式是重构的，来源并不完全确定。

items.en: Old French parfournir meant to complete or carry out fully, joining par- with fournir.
items.cn: 古法语 parfournir 意为「彻底完成、履行」，由 par- 与 fournir 组合而成。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as performen, first meaning to accomplish a task and later to act a role or play music.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 performen，先指完成任务，后来才指扮演角色或演奏音乐。

items.en: The suffix -er was added to name the person, and by the sixteenth century performer covered both stage artists and people who carry out duties.
items.cn: 加上后缀 -er 用来指人，到十六世纪 performer 已同时指舞台艺人与履行职责的人。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same verb; the near-meaning group collects the kinds of people who stand in front of an audience.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一动词上的词；近义组收各类站在观众面前的人。

entries.definition: To carry out an action, or to act, sing or play for an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 执行某项行动；也指为观众表演、演唱或演奏。

entries.definition: The act of performing, or how well someone or something does.
entries.definitionCN: 表演这一行为；也指某人或某物的表现。

entries.definition: The adjective describing arts or actions that are performed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容需要当众表演的艺术或动作。

entries.definition: Relating to language or behaviour that does something by being said or done.
entries.definitionCN: 形容言语或行为本身即在完成某事的；述行性的。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to amuse an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 以娱乐观众为职业的人。

entries.definition: A person who creates or performs art.
entries.definitionCN: 从事艺术创作或表演的人。

entries.definition: A person who performs a role in a play or film.
entries.definitionCN: 在戏剧或电影中扮演角色的人。

entries.definition: A person who plays or writes music.
entries.definitionCN: 演奏或创作音乐的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is the verb plus the person suffix, and the verb still carries the older idea of finishing what was started.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是动词加「做某事的人」后缀，而动词本身仍带着「把开始的事做完」这个更早的意思。

normal.en: Perform plus -er makes the doer: the person who performs.
normal.cn: perform 加 -er 造出动作的执行者，也就是表演的人。

normal.en: The -er here works exactly as in singer, dancer and teacher.
normal.cn: 这里的 -er 与 singer、dancer、teacher 里的 -er 作用完全相同。

normal.en: Perform came from Old French parfournir, to carry out fully, and only later took the stage sense.
normal.cn: perform 来自古法语 parfournir，意为彻底完成，舞台义是后来才有的。

normal.en: Performance is the act, performer is the person: the pair fills two slots of the same event.
normal.cn: performance 指行为，performer 指人，两者正好填满同一件事的两个位置。

normal.en: A good performer in a business report means a product that sells well, not a singer.
normal.cn: 商业报告里的 good performer 指卖得好的产品，不是歌手。

abstract.en: Think of the moment a person crosses from the dark wings into the light: that single step makes an ordinary person a performer.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人从昏暗的侧幕走进灯光的那一瞬间，这一步就把普通人变成了表演者。

abstract.en: Any job done in public turns the worker into a performer, which is why the word slides so easily into business talk.
abstract.cn: 任何在众人面前完成的活都会让干活的人带上表演性质，这就是这个词能轻易滑进商业用语的原因。

abstract.en: The word pairs a finished action with a human body, so it always asks two questions: what was done, and who did it.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一个完成的动作和一具人的身体绑在一起，所以它总在问两件事：做了什么，以及谁做的。

examples.en: The performer bowed twice before leaving the stage.
examples.cn: 这位表演者鞠了两次躬才离开舞台。

examples.en: A good performer listens to the room as much as to the script.
examples.cn: 好的表演者听台下的反应，和听台词一样认真。

examples.en: The new engine is a strong performer in cold weather.
examples.cn: 这款新发动机在低温下表现强劲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼佛么」——他一开口就把情绪泼满全场，观众直问这是哪来的佛么；记住 performer 是表演者。

root: 英语动词 perform 加后缀 -er 构成；perform 一般认为来自古法语 parfournir（彻底完成），词首 per- 来自拉丁语，词干 fournir 源自法兰克语，来源不完全确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is someone who carries an action through; the senses then split between the stage, the workplace and any object judged by results.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把某个动作完成到底的人；义项由此分为舞台上的表演者、工作中的执行者，以及任何按表现好坏来评价的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single figure stepping out of the wings into a pool of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人从侧幕走出，踏进一小片灯光里。

branches.en: a singer bowing under a single spotlight
branches.cn: 聚光灯下鞠躬的歌手

branches.en: a dancer counting the beat in the wings
branches.cn: 侧幕里数着节拍的舞者

branches.en: a clerk who finishes every item on the list
branches.cn: 把清单每一项都做完的职员

branches.en: a company praised for strong quarterly numbers
branches.cn: 因季度业绩亮眼而受称赞的公司

branches.en: a machine that does its job and does it well
branches.cn: 既完成任务又完成得漂亮的机器

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix plus a Frankish stem, passed through French, then closed with an English suffix that names the person.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语前缀加法兰克语词干，经法语传来，最后加一个指人的英语后缀收尾。

latinIntro.en: Only the prefix per- is Latin; the verb stem reached English from Frankish through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前缀 per- 属于拉丁语；动词词干是经古法语从法兰克语进入英语的。

items.meaning: to carry out; to act or play for an audience

definition_zh: 也许；或许；可能；大概
definition_en: used to say that something may be true or may happen, or to make a suggestion, request or estimate sound softer
core_image: 一枚硬币还在空中旋转，正反两面都还握在手里
scene: 雨点敲着窗，朋友问晚上要不要出门，你还没有拿定主意。Perhaps we should stay in and cook something simple.
sceneCN: 这里是「也许、可能」（第 1 个义项：表示不确定的可能性）；句意为也许今晚该待在家里做点简单的饭菜。

derivatives.zh: 与 perhaps 共享表示「运气、机会」的词干 hap，义为「发生；碰巧」
hap 加前缀 mis- 构成，义为「小事故；不幸」，与 perhaps 同源
hap 与 hazard 复合，义为「偶然的；杂乱的」，与 perhaps 同源

senses.title: Something may be true or may happen
senses.definition: used to say that something may be the case or may happen, without saying that it will
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事可能是真的或可能发生，但并不保证会发生
senses.example: Perhaps the train is late because of the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 也许火车是因为下雪才晚点的。
senses.why: The word began as a phrase meaning by chance, so its first job is to mark a possibility sitting between yes and no.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是「凭运气」的说法，所以它最基本的用途是标出一种停在「是」与「否」之间的可能性。

senses.title: A softened request or suggestion
senses.definition: used to make a suggestion, request or opinion sound less direct and less forceful
senses.definitionCN: 用于让建议、请求或看法听起来不那么直接、不那么强硬
senses.example: Perhaps you could send the file before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 或许你可以在周五之前把文件发过来。
senses.why: If a claim only describes a chance, the speaker cannot be accused of pushing too hard, so the same word becomes a polite way to ask for something.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个说法只描述「有可能」，说话人就不算把话说满，于是同一个词变成了客气地提出请求的方式。

senses.title: An approximate number
senses.definition: used before a number to show that it is an estimate rather than an exact figure
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字前，表示那是估出来的数目而非精确数字
senses.example: Perhaps forty people came to the talk.
senses.exampleCN: 大概有四十个人来听了那场讲座。
senses.why: An estimate is just a possible figure rather than a measured one, which is the same hedge applied to quantity instead of to truth.
senses.whyCN: 估出来的数字只是「可能如此」的数目，而不是量出来的，这等于把同样的不确定从真假挪到了数量上。

intro.en: Perhaps is a worn-down English phrase: a Latin preposition joined to an old Norse noun for luck and written as one word.
intro.cn: perhaps 是一个磨平了的英语短语：一个拉丁语介词接上一个表示运气的古诺斯语名词，最后写成了一个词。

items.en: Latin per meant through or by, and it is still visible in phrases such as per cent.
items.cn: 拉丁语 per 意为「经由、凭」，在 per cent 这类短语里仍能看见。

items.en: Old Norse happ meant chance or good luck, and English kept it as the noun hap.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 happ 意为「机会、好运」，英语把它保留为名词 hap。

items.en: Middle English put the two together as the phrase per hap, literally by chance.
items.cn: 中古英语把两者合为短语 per hap，字面意思就是「凭运气」。

items.en: The phrase was written as one word, first as perhappes or perhapse, before the modern spelling settled.
items.cn: 这个短语被写成一个词，先作 perhappes 或 perhapse，之后才固定成现代拼写。

items.en: Modern English uses perhaps as a single adverb of possibility, while the old noun hap survives mainly inside compounds.
items.cn: 现代英语把 perhaps 当作一个表示可能性的副词，旧名词 hap 主要残留在复合词里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words sharing the old noun for luck; the near-meaning group collects adverbs that also mark possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「运气」这个旧名词的词；近义组收同样标记可能性的副词。

entries.definition: An old word for chance or luck, now rare outside compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 表示机会或运气的古词，如今主要残留在复合词中。

entries.definition: To take place, especially by chance.
entries.definitionCN: 发生，尤指偶然发生。

entries.definition: Arranged without plan or order.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无计划或秩序地安排的；杂乱的。

entries.definition: A small accident or piece of bad luck.
entries.definitionCN: 小事故；不幸的意外。

entries.definition: Possibly; used to say that something may be the case.
entries.definitionCN: 也许；用于表示某事可能如此。

entries.definition: Used when something is possible but not certain.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表示有可能但不确定。

entries.definition: Used when something is more likely than not.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表示可能性较大；很可能。

entries.definition: In a way that can be imagined as possible.
entries.definitionCN: 可以想象为可能的；或许。

normalIntro.en: The word still shows its two pieces: a preposition of means and an old noun for luck.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词至今还露着两块零件：一个表示「凭借」的介词，和一个表示运气的旧名词。

normal.en: Per hap literally says by chance, which is exactly what the adverb still does.
normal.cn: per hap 字面就是「凭运气」，这正是这个副词今天仍在做的事。

normal.en: Hap is an old word for luck, and it lives on in happen, haphazard and mishap.
normal.cn: hap 是表示运气的古词，如今活在 happen、haphazard 和 mishap 里。

normal.en: Latin per means through or by, as in per cent, by the hundred.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 per 意为「经由、凭」，如 per cent 就是「按百计算」。

normal.en: Perhaps and maybe do the same job, but perhaps is the more written and more formal of the two.
normal.cn: perhaps 与 maybe 作用相同，但 perhaps 更偏书面、更正式。

normal.en: At the head of a sentence, perhaps usually softens a suggestion rather than expressing real doubt.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，perhaps 多半是在软化建议，而不是真的表示怀疑。

abstract.en: Keep the coin spinning in the air: while it turns, both faces are still possible, and that is the whole meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象那枚还在空中旋转的硬币：转着的时候正反两面都还可能，这就是这个词的全部意思。

abstract.en: A hedge is not a lie and not a promise, and perhaps is the little hedge people plant around a claim.
abstract.cn: 含糊其辞既不是撒谎也不是承诺，perhaps 就是人们在说法周围种下的一小圈篱笆。

abstract.en: The word costs the speaker almost nothing, yet it leaves room for the listener to disagree without a fight.
abstract.cn: 这个词几乎不花说话人什么代价，却给听者留出了不伤和气地反对的余地。

examples.en: Perhaps the rain will stop before we leave.
examples.cn: 也许我们出发前雨会停。

examples.en: Perhaps you should ask the manager directly.
examples.cn: 或许你该直接去问经理。

examples.en: There were perhaps twenty people in the room.
examples.cn: 房间里大概有二十个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕哈普斯」——心里没底就怕说错，先加一句也许垫着；记住 perhaps 是或许。

root: 中古英语短语 per hap，字面义为「凭运气」；per 来自拉丁语 per（经由），hap 来自古诺斯语 happ（运气、机会），同源词还有 happen、mishap。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a possibility held open; the senses then spread to polite suggestions and to rough estimates of number.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一种悬着不定的可能性；义项由此扩展到委婉的建议和粗略的数字估计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin still spinning in the air, neither face settled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币还在空中旋转，哪一面都还没落定。

branches.en: a coin still spinning in the air
branches.cn: 还在空中旋转的硬币

branches.en: a cloud that may or may not bring rain
branches.cn: 说不准会不会下雨的云

branches.en: a note passed quietly to a colleague
branches.cn: 悄悄递给同事的一张便条

branches.en: a rough count made on the fingers
branches.cn: 用手指粗略点数

branches.en: a forecast that speaks of likely showers
branches.cn: 说可能有阵雨的天气预报

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin preposition of means and an old Norse noun for luck, written as one unit only in English.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示「凭借」的拉丁语介词和一个表示运气的古诺斯语名词拼成，只有英语把它写成了一个单位。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies only the preposition per; the noun hap is Germanic, borrowed from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只提供了介词 per；名词 hap 属于日耳曼语，借自古诺斯语。

definition_zh: 时期；阶段；周期；课时；句号；经期
definition_en: a length of time, a stage in history or a process, a recurring cycle, a lesson, or the full stop at the end of a sentence
core_image: 一条走了一圈又回到原点的轨道：起点与终点重合，中间那段就是一圈。
scene: 维多利亚时代，世界上第一批地下铁路开始运行。The Victorian period saw the first underground railways in the world.
sceneCN: 这里 period 是「历史上的一段时期」（第 2 个义项：时代、阶段）；句意：维多利亚时期出现了世界上最早的地下铁路。场景要点：煤气灯、砖砌车站、旧式火车；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 时期；阶段；周期；课时；句号；经期
某一时代的；仿古的（如 period furniture）

collocations.zh: 时代风格的作品；古装作品

derivatives.zh: 周期的；定期发生的
期刊；定期出版的
定期地；周期性地
周期性

senses.title: A length of time with limits
senses.definition: a length of time during which something happens, especially one with a clear beginning and end
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生所经历的一段时间，尤指有明确起止的
senses.example: The study covered a period of five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究覆盖了五年时间。
senses.why: Greek periodos was 'a going around', from peri 'around' + hodos 'way'. A measured stretch of time is a closed loop with a start and a finish.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 periodos 是“绕行一周”，由 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路”构成。被量出的一段时光，就是一个有起点和终点的闭环。

senses.title: A stage of history
senses.definition: a particular stretch of history with its own character, style, or events
senses.definitionCN: 具有自身特征、风格或事件的历史阶段
senses.example: The country changed its alphabet twice in that period.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在那个时期两次更换文字。
senses.why: History is cut into loops: a culture goes through a way of doing things and comes out the other side, leaving a named stretch behind.
senses.whyCN: 历史被切成一圈一圈：一种文化走完一套做法，从另一边出来，留下一段被命名的时光。

senses.title: A recurring cycle
senses.definition: a regular interval after which an event or process repeats
senses.definitionCN: 某一事件或过程重复出现所间隔的固定时间
senses.example: The comet returns every 76 years, its orbital period.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗彗星每 76 年回归一次，这就是它的轨道周期。
senses.why: This is the most literal sense: a body goes around and comes back to the same place. The interval is the time the loop takes.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的义项：一个物体绕行一圈，回到同一位置。这个间隔就是那一圈所花的时间。

senses.title: One lesson in a school day
senses.definition: one of the fixed blocks of time into which a school day is divided
senses.definitionCN: 学校一天被划分成的若干个固定时间段之一
senses.example: We have two periods of chemistry on Tuesdays.
senses.exampleCN: 我们周二有两节化学课。
senses.why: The school day is cut into loops of equal length. Each block is a period because it is a closed, measured unit that ends when the bell rings.
senses.whyCN: 学校的一天被切成等长的圈。每一格都是 period，因为它是一个封闭的、被量出的单位，铃响就结束。

senses.title: The full stop in punctuation
senses.definition: the mark at the end of a declarative sentence
senses.definitionCN: 陈述句末尾的那个标点
senses.example: Delete the extra period at the end of the citation.
senses.exampleCN: 删掉引文末尾多余的那个句号。
senses.why: Recorded from the 1580s. A sentence is a loop of thought; the full stop closes the loop, which is why the mark took the name of a completed cycle.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 80 年代见于记录。一个句子是一圈思想；句号把这一圈合上，所以这个符号借用了“完成一个周期”的名字。

senses.title: Menstruation
senses.titleCN: 经期：按月转回的那几天
senses.definition: the monthly bleeding cycle in a person who menstruates, or the time it lasts
senses.definitionCN: 有月经的人每月一次的出血周期，或该周期持续的几天
senses.example: The app tracks the length of each period.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用记录每次经期的长度。
senses.why: Recorded from 1822. The bodily cycle returns at a regular interval, so the medical use simply names the most visible human example of a period.
senses.whyCN: 1822 年见于记录。身体周期按固定间隔转回来，医学用法只是把人类最可见的一个“周期”例子叫成了 period。

senses.title: One division of a sports game
senses.titleCN: 比赛分节：把一场球切成几段
senses.definition: one of the equal parts into which a game such as ice hockey is divided
senses.definitionCN: 冰球等比赛中把整场划分成的若干个等长时间段之一
senses.example: They scored twice in the second period.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在第二节里进了两球。
senses.why: A game is another closed stretch of time divided into loops. Each period starts with a face-off and ends with a whistle.
senses.whyCN: 一场比赛也是一段被切成若干圈的封闭时间。每一节从开球开始，到哨响结束。

senses.title: Belonging to a past style
senses.titleCN: 仿古的：带着某个时代的样子
senses.definition: of furniture, costume, or a work, made in or imitating the style of a particular historical period
senses.definitionCN: 指家具、服装或作品按某一历史时期的风格制作或仿制
senses.example: The room was furnished with period pieces from the 1780s.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里摆着 1780 年代的仿古家具。
senses.why: The noun becomes an adjective: an object carries the look of a named loop of history, so it is 'period' rather than merely old.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为形容词：一件物品带着某段被命名的历史圈的样子，所以它是“时期的”，而不只是“旧的”。

intro.en: Period is Greek periodos 'a going around', from peri 'around' + hodos 'way'. English borrowed it through Latin and first used it for a cycle of time.
intro.cn: period 是希腊语 periodos“绕行一周”，由 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路”构成。英语经拉丁语借入，最早用来指时间的循环。

items.en: Hodos meant 'way, road, journey'. It survives in English compounds such as method ('a way along') and period.
items.cn: hodos 意为“路、道路、行程”。它保留在英语的 method（“沿路而行”）与 period 等复合词里。

items.en: Periodos meant 'a going around, a circuit, a cycle', used of the sun's course and of rhetorical sentences that round off.
items.cn: periodos 意为“绕行、一圈、循环”，用于太阳的运行，也用于首尾完整、能收口的修辞句子。

items.en: Latin took periodus as a term of astronomy and rhetoric. Its sense of a rounded sentence is why the closing mark later took this name.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 periodus 作为天文学与修辞学术语使用。它“首尾完整的句子”这一义，正是后来收尾标点取这个名字的原因。

items.en: English records period around 1400 meaning 'course, extent of time, cycle'. The historical sense 'a named age' develops from this.
items.cn: 英语在 1400 年前后记录 period，意为“进程、时间长度、周期”。历史的“被命名的时代”义由此发展而来。

items.en: The punctuation sense is recorded in the 1580s. A full stop is literally the mark that closes the period of a sentence.
items.cn: 标点义于 16 世纪 80 年代见于记录。句号字面上就是“合上一句话的那一圈”的记号。

items.en: The menstrual sense is recorded from 1822, and the school and sports senses follow the same model: a day or a game cut into closed blocks of time.
items.cn: 经期义于 1822 年见于记录；课时与比赛分节义遵循同样的模式：把一天或一场比赛切成封闭的时间块。

note.en: The first group is the period family plus compounds built on it; the second collects words for stretches of time.
note.cn: 第一组是 period 词族及由它构成的复合词；第二组收“时间段”类近义词。

entries.definition: happening at regular intervals, or relating to a period. It is the adjective of period, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔发生的；与周期有关的。它是 period 的形容词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: a magazine published at regular intervals, or published regularly. The noun sense is a publication, not a time span.
entries.definitionCN: 定期出版的杂志；定期出版的。名词指出版物，不是时间段。

entries.definition: an object or work valued for its style from a past era. Here period works as an adjective meaning 'of a historical era'.
entries.definitionCN: 因带有过去时代风格而有价值的物品或作品。这里 period 作形容词，意为“某一历史时代的”。

entries.definition: the quality of occurring in regular cycles. It names the abstract property behind periodic.
entries.definitionCN: 按规律周期发生的性质。它命名 periodic 背后的抽象属性。

entries.definition: a long period of history named after a system, leader, or event. It is usually larger and more formal than period.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种制度、领袖或事件命名的长历史阶段。它通常比 period 更大、更正式。

entries.definition: a period that begins with a striking change and is treated as a new starting point. It stresses the break, not just the length.
entries.definitionCN: 以显著变化开始、被视为新起点的时期。它强调断裂，而不只是长度。

entries.definition: a long stretch of history associated with a way of life, as in the Bronze Age or the age of the internet. It is looser than period.
entries.definitionCN: 与某种生活方式相关联的长历史阶段，如青铜时代、互联网时代。它比 period 宽松。

entries.definition: a fixed length of time for which something lasts, such as a school term or a prison term. It is defined by an agreement or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物持续的固定时长，如学期、刑期。它由约定或规则界定。

entries.definition: a short period of a particular activity or weather. It is informal and almost always short.
entries.definitionCN: 某活动或天气的一小段。它口语化，且几乎总是很短。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Greek peri 'around' + hodos 'way', giving periodos 'a going around'. Family words periodic, periodical, periodically, periodicity, and compounds period piece and grace period.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：希腊语 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路”，合成 periodos“绕行一周”。词族为 periodic、periodical、periodically、periodicity，以及复合词 period piece、grace period。

normal.en: Period and method share hodos 'way': one is a way around, the other a way along.
normal.cn: period 与 method 共享 hodos“路”：一个是绕一圈的路，一个是沿着走的路。

normal.en: A full stop is called a period because it closes the sentence's circuit.
normal.cn: 句号叫 period，是因为它把句子的回路合上。

normal.en: A school day is cut into periods the way a circle is cut into arcs.
normal.cn: 学校的一天被切成 period，就像圆被切成弧。

normal.en: Periodic table: elements arranged by repeating cycles of properties.
normal.cn: 元素周期表：按性质重复的周期排列元素。

normal.en: A period piece is an object still wearing the clothes of its era.
normal.cn: period piece 是一件还穿着它那个时代衣服的物品。

abstract.en: History is only manageable because we agree to cut it into loops.
abstract.cn: 历史之所以可处理，只是因为我们同意把它切成一圈一圈。

abstract.en: A period is a promise that the sentence will end.
abstract.cn: 句号是一个承诺：这句话会结束。

abstract.en: Every cycle is a way of saying that the same place can be reached again.
abstract.cn: 每一个周期，都是在说同一个地方还能再被抵达。

examples.en: Sales rose sharply over the same period last year.
examples.cn: 销售额在去年同期那段时期大幅上升。

examples.en: The teacher gave us ten minutes at the end of the period.
examples.cn: 老师在那一节课末尾给了我们十分钟。

examples.en: Put a period at the end of every complete sentence.
examples.cn: 每个完整的句子末尾都要加句号。

dict_mnemonic.text: “皮瑞尔的”——皮瑞尔的怀表每绕一圈就响一次，一圈就是一段 → period 周期、时期

root: 源自希腊语 periodos“绕行一周”，由 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路、行程”构成；经拉丁语 periodus、古法语进入英语，约 1400 年义为“进程、时长、周期”。核心是“绕一圈所花的那段时间”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of period, all one shape: a closed stretch that begins, runs its course, and comes back to an end.
sensesIntro.cn: period 的八个义项是同一个形状：一段封闭的时间，开始、走完、回到终点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a track that leaves a point, goes all the way around, and returns to the same point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从某点出发、绕行一圈、又回到同一点的轨道。

branches.en: SPAN: from a five-year study to the Victorian age, every span is a loop someone has marked off.
branches.cn: 跨度：从五年的研究到维多利亚时代，每一段都是有人划出的一圈。

branches.en: REPETITION: an orbit and a hockey game both return to the start on a schedule.
branches.cn: 重复：轨道与冰球比赛，都按时刻表回到起点。

branches.en: BODY AND SCHOOL: the timetable and the monthly cycle are the same closed block imposed on living time.
branches.cn: 身体与学校：课表与月度周期，都是加在活的时间上的同一种封闭块。

branches.en: PUNCTUATION: the mark that closes a sentence borrows the name of a completed circuit.
branches.cn: 标点：合上句子的符号，借用了“完成一圈”的名字。

branches.en: STYLE: an object can still carry the look of the loop it was made in.
branches.cn: 风格：一件物品仍然带着它被造出时那一圈的样子。

intro.en: Period's family is built on the Greek compound periodos. Suffixes turn it into an adjective, an adverb, and a noun of property; compounds name the things people measure in cycles.
intro.cn: period 的词族建立在希腊复合词 periodos 上。后缀把它变成形容词、副词与属性名词；复合词则命名人们按周期计量的东西。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are Greek hodos 'way', periodos 'circuit', and Latin periodus, the borrowing English received. Latin added no new root.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是希腊语 hodos“路”、periodos“一圈”与拉丁语借形 periodus，英语承接的正是后者。拉丁语没有新增词根。

items.meaning: occurring at regular intervals; relating to a period
items.meaningCN: 按固定间隔发生的；与周期有关的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The system runs a periodic backup every night.
items.exampleCN: 系统每晚执行一次定期备份。

items.meaning: published at regular intervals; a magazine so published

items.example: The library keeps back issues of the periodical.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆保存这份期刊的过刊。

items.meaningCN: 定期地；周期性地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: the quality of recurring in cycles
items.meaningCN: 按周期重复的性质（-ity 构成属性名词）
items.example: The periodicity of the signal suggests a rotating source.
items.exampleCN: 信号的周期性表明源头在旋转。

items.meaning: a work or object valued for its historical style
items.meaningCN: 因历史风格而有价值的作品或物品
items.example: The film is a period piece set in 1912.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影是设定在 1912 年的年代戏。

items.meaning: extra time allowed before a penalty applies
items.meaningCN: 在处罚生效前额外允许的时间
items.example: The bank offers a ten-day grace period.

items.meaning: a particular stretch of time being discussed
items.meaningCN: 正在讨论的某一特定时间段
items.example: Over this time period, prices doubled.
items.exampleCN: 在这段时间里，价格上涨了一倍。

items.example: She takes two days off for period pain each month.
items.exampleCN: 她每月因经期疼痛休息两天。

items.meaning: the arrangement of elements by repeating chemical properties
items.meaningCN: 按化学性质重复规律排列元素的表格
items.example: Carbon sits in the second row of the periodic table.
items.exampleCN: 碳位于元素周期表第二行。

items.meaning: clothing made in the style of a historical era
items.meaningCN: 按历史时期风格制作的服装
items.example: The actors wore period costume in every scene.
items.exampleCN: 演员在每一场都穿年代服装。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 一圈；完整的句子；时间周期

senses.title: Lasting indefinitely
senses.definition: lasting forever or with no fixed end
senses.definitionCN: 永远存在或没有确定终点
senses.example: The treaty made the river a permanent boundary.
senses.exampleCN: 条约使这条河成为永久边界。
senses.why: Latin permanere means to remain through to the end, and the present participle fixes that staying into a quality.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 permanere 意为「一直留到最后」，现在分词把这层「留住」定成品性。

senses.title: Long-lasting rather than temporary
senses.definition: intended to last a long time, in contrast with a temporary arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 打算长期维持，与临时安排相对
senses.example: They moved into a permanent office after the trial year.
senses.exampleCN: 试行一年后，他们搬进了长期办公室。
senses.why: Everyday use softens forever into for the foreseeable future.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法把「永远」软化为「可预见的将来」。

senses.title: A regular staff position
senses.definition: holding a post with a settled contract rather than a short-term one
senses.definitionCN: 持有稳定合同的岗位，而非短期岗位
senses.example: She was offered a permanent post in the department.
senses.exampleCN: 系里给了她一个正式职位。
senses.why: Employment law turns the word into a boundary between contract types.
senses.whyCN: 劳动法把这个词变成合同类型之间的界限。

senses.title: A material that does not fade
senses.definition: marking a material whose colour or mark is meant to stay
senses.definitionCN: 标记一种颜色或印记不易消失的材料
senses.example: He labelled the box with a permanent marker.
senses.exampleCN: 他用不褪色记号笔在箱子上做了标记。
senses.why: The adjective moves from the arrangement to the stuff that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从安排转到承载安排的材质上。

senses.title: A long-holding wave
senses.definition: a hairstyle whose curl is meant to last for months
senses.definitionCN: 卷发效果能维持数月的发型
senses.example: She asked the stylist for a permanent before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出行前她请理发师给她烫个发。
senses.why: The trade noun keeps the promise of duration in a small everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 行业里的名词把「持久」的承诺放进一个日常小义。

senses.title: A resident status
senses.definition: the legal right to live in a country without time limit
senses.definitionCN: 在一国无限期居住的合法权利
senses.example: He applied for permanent residence after five years.
senses.exampleCN: 五年后他申请了永久居留。
senses.why: Immigration law needs a term for the strongest form of stay.
senses.whyCN: 移民法需要一个词指最稳固的居留形式。

senses.title: Irreversible harm
senses.definition: damage that will not heal or be undone
senses.definitionCN: 不会痊愈或被撤销的损害
senses.example: The frost caused permanent damage to the buds.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻对花芽造成了永久性损害。
senses.why: The word marks the point where repair stops being possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出修复不再可能的那一点。

senses.title: A lasting record
senses.definition: an official record that is kept indefinitely
senses.definitionCN: 无限期保存的正式记录
senses.example: The offence stayed on his permanent record.
senses.exampleCN: 这项过错留在了他的永久档案里。
senses.why: Bureaucracy uses the word to say that erasure is not allowed.
senses.whyCN: 行政系统用这个词表示不允许抹除。

intro.en: Permanent comes from Latin permanens, the present participle of permanere, to remain throughout, built on per- through and manere to stay. Both parts are clear.
intro.cn: permanent 来自拉丁 permanens，即 permanere「一直留到最后」的现在分词，由 per-「贯穿」与 manere「停留」构成。两部分都清楚。

items.en: Manere meant to stay, remain or dwell, and it also gives mansion and manor through French.
items.cn: manere 意为停留、留下、居住，经法语也给出 mansion 与 manor。

items.en: Per- means through or throughout, so permanere is to stay through the whole span.
items.cn: per- 意为贯穿、始终，因此 permanere 是在整段时间里一直留下。

items.en: The present participle permanens described a thing that keeps its place or state.
items.cn: 现在分词 permanens 描述保持位置或状态的事物。

items.en: English took permanent in the late Middle Ages; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期借入 permanent，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Permanence and permanency name the state, while impermanent adds a Latin negative prefix.
items.cn: permanence 与 permanency 命名状态，impermanent 则加拉丁否定前缀。

items.en: The word now also names a hairstyle, a marker and a residence status.
items.cn: 这个词如今还指一种发型、一种记号笔与一种居留身份。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin stay-root; the second group names duration and stability.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「停留」词根；第二组是表示持续与稳定的近义说法。

entries.definition: The state of lasting or remaining unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 持久或保持不变的状态。

entries.definition: In a way that is meant to last.
entries.definitionCN: 以打算长久维持的方式。

entries.definition: Not lasting; the negative form built with im-.
entries.definitionCN: 不持久的；用 im- 构成的否定形式。

entries.definition: To stay behind or continue in a place, from the same Latin verb through French.
entries.definitionCN: 留下或继续在某处，经法语出自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: A large house, from the Latin idea of dwelling.
entries.definitionCN: 大宅，出自拉丁语「居住」的观念。

entries.definition: Continuing for a long time, without implying forever.
entries.definitionCN: 持续很久，但不含「永远」。

entries.definition: Lasting through hardship or time.
entries.definitionCN: 历经困难或时间仍持续。

entries.definition: Continuing without interruption, often stronger than permanent.
entries.definitionCN: 不间断地持续，语气常比 permanent 更强。

entries.definition: Set in place and not changing.
entries.definitionCN: 固定就位、不再改变。

entries.definition: Steady and not likely to move or fail.
entries.definitionCN: 稳定，不易移动或失效。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Manere is to stay, and per- is through, so permanent is to stay through the whole span.
normal.cn: manere 是停留，per- 是贯穿，所以 permanent 是整段时间都留下。

normal.en: Mansion and manor come from the same dwelling word.
normal.cn: mansion 与 manor 出自同一个「居住」词。

normal.en: Impermanent is the negative: im- plus permanent.
normal.cn: impermanent 是反义：im- 加 permanent。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: permanent residence, permanent job, permanent damage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：永久居留、正式工作、永久损害。

normal.en: A permanent marker keeps its mark; a permanent wave keeps its curl.
normal.cn: 不褪色记号笔留住字迹，烫发留住卷度。

abstract.en: Permanent is a stone carved with letters that outlast the hand that cut them.
abstract.cn: 永久是石头上凿的字，比刻字的手活得更久。

abstract.en: The word promises duration without naming an end, which is why lawyers argue over it.
abstract.cn: 这个词承诺持续却不说明终点，所以律师总要争它。

abstract.en: To call a thing permanent is to bet that time will not revise it.
abstract.cn: 称某物为永久，就是赌时间不会改写它。

examples.en: The bridge was built as a permanent crossing, not a seasonal one.
examples.cn: 这座桥建成永久通道，而非季节性设施。

examples.en: A permanent loss of hearing followed the explosion.
examples.cn: 爆炸之后出现了永久性听力丧失。

examples.en: The museum keeps a permanent collection in the east wing.
examples.cn: 博物馆在东翼设有永久藏品。

root: 拉丁 permanens「一直留下的」← permanere「留到最后」← per-「贯穿」+ manere「停留、居住」。manere 经法语也给出 mansion 与 manor；英语中世纪晚期借入 permanent，确切首见年代不确定。permanence 指状态，impermanent 由 im- 否定；现代另有烫发、不褪色记号笔与永久居留等专义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from endless duration to long arrangements, posts, materials, hairstyles, statuses, harm and records.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从无限持续，转到长期安排、职位、材料、发型、身份、损害与档案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: letters cut into stone, still readable after decades of rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：凿进石头的字，几十年雨水之后仍可辨认。

branches.en: THE ENDLESS STAY: duration with no fixed end.
branches.cn: 没有终点的停留：没有确定终点的持续。

branches.en: THE LONG ARRANGEMENT: what is meant to outlast a trial period.
branches.cn: 长期安排：打算熬过试行期的安排。

branches.en: THE SETTLED STATUS: a staff post and a residence right.
branches.cn: 稳固的身份：正式职位与居留权利。

branches.en: THE FIXED MARK: ink that does not fade and a curl that holds.
branches.cn: 固定的印记：不褪的字迹与持久的卷度。

branches.en: THE UNCHANGING RECORD: harm that cannot be undone and a file that is never erased.
branches.cn: 不可改的记录：无法撤销的损害与永不抹除的档案。

intro.en: Permanent is Latin permanens plus the English adjective ending; the verb permanere carries both per- and manere.
intro.cn: permanent 是拉丁 permanens 加英语形容词词尾；动词 permanere 同时带着 per- 与 manere。

latinIntro.en: Manere gives the stay-root, per- carries it through time, and permanens supplies the participle behind the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: manere 提供「停留」词根，per- 让它贯穿时间，permanens 提供英语形容词背后的分词。

items.example: The prefix stretches the stay across the whole span.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把「停留」拉满整段时间。

items.example: The verb is the plain act of remaining.
items.exampleCN: 动词就是「留下」这一平实动作。

items.structure: Latin verb, compound of per- and manere
items.example: Latin joined the two parts into one verb.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把两部分合成一个动词。

items.example: The participle turns the act into a quality.
The noun names the state the participle describes.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名分词所描述的状态。

items.example: English keeps the participle ending as -ent.
items.exampleCN: 英语把分词词尾保留为 -ent。

items.example: The noun is the abstract partner of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 名词是形容词的抽象搭档。

items.example: The adverb marks how long something is meant to stay.
items.exampleCN: 副词标出打算维持多久。

items.example: The prefix makes impermanent, the negative partner.
items.exampleCN: 前缀构成 impermanent 这一否定搭档。

items.example: The negative keeps the same stay-root.
items.exampleCN: 否定形式沿用同一「停留」词根。
